commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to Lizzy
Echo commands until Lizzy receives bye
Allow Lizzy tasks to be unmarked
Represent Level-3 tasks with Task objects
Add reusable console UI testing skill
commitResults.messageBody: Document UI scenarios and require agents to maintain and run them after code updates.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add todo deadline and event task support
commitResults.messageBody: Represent task types and date-time details without inheritance, with console UI coverage.
Use Todo, Deadline, and Event subclasses while retaining a shared Task array and matching the approved UI wording.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add UI tests for invalid task commands
commitResults.messageBody: Cover empty lists, out-of-range status updates, and malformed dated-task commands so future validation preserves task-list state after rejected input.
Store tasks in an ArrayList so indexed deletion reindexes the list naturally, and cover delete plus whitespace and empty-list edge cases.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save task changes to a relative data file
commitResults.messageBody: Persist the complete task list after each mutation and create the data directory automatically so first-time runs work across operating systems. Isolate UI test data and verify the serialized completion state.

commitResults.messageTitle: Load saved tasks when Lizzy starts
commitResults.messageBody: Restore every task type and completion state from the relative data file. Treat a missing file as a first run, create missing folders on save, and explain malformed or inaccessible storage without crashing.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch-Level-7 for persistent task storage
commitResults.messageBody: Preserve the Level 7 branch history while bringing automatic save/load behavior and corruption handling into master.
Store deadline and event dates as calendar values, require ISO yyyy-MM-dd input, display readable dates, reject impossible dates and reversed event ranges, and preserve parsed dates through storage.
Add an on command that lists deadlines on an exact date and events spanning that date, while retaining original task numbers and handling empty or malformed date queries.
Preserve the Level 8 branch history while bringing LocalDate parsing, readable formatting, and date-based schedule lookup into master.

Move command reading and all user-facing messages out of Lizzy so the application coordinator no longer prints directly. This keeps the existing console contract while giving later commands a focused UI dependency.
Move task storage, one-based lookup, deletion, and task-number validation out of Lizzy. Provide immutable snapshots to Storage while retaining all user-facing behavior.

Move command splitting, syntax validation, task construction, date parsing, and input error messages out of Lizzy. Keep Lizzy focused on coordinating parsed commands with the task list, UI, and storage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Dispatch user requests through Command objects
commitResults.messageBody: Have Parser construct executable command objects for each supported request. Move task mutations, persistence, and result presentation into focused Command subclasses, leaving Lizzy responsible only for application lifecycle and error handling.

Group commands, tasks, parsing, storage, UI, and exceptions by responsibility while preserving src/main/java as the source root. Update launch and test paths, rename OnCommand for clarity, and expose task dates for cross-package persistence access.
Set the Gradle application entry point and shadow JAR name to match the packaged Lizzy application.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit coverage for core Lizzy behavior
commitResults.messageBody: Cover parser validation, task-list operations, persistence, completion state, and schedule matching. Document the high-value 50% coverage target for future changes.
Explain how to build Lizzy's Shadow fat JAR, locate it, and run it from a separate folder.

commitResults.messageTitle: Complete JavaDoc coverage for Lizzy APIs
commitResults.messageBody: Document all public classes, constructors, and methods with contracts, and add detailed documentation for non-trivial private helpers.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add SE-EDU Java coding standard skill
commitResults.messageBody:
Future Java changes need a shared project-specific reference for the
SE-EDU intermediate conventions.

Add concise guidance for naming, layout, documentation, and validation
without duplicating the external guide.

Future repository operations need a shared project-specific reference
for the SE-EDU Git conventions.

Add focused guidance for branch names, commit messages, and
authorized history changes.

Future Java and Git work needs to consistently follow the project
standards skills.

Mandate the Java skill for source changes and the Git skill for
repository operations while preserving user-specified workflows.

The source uses compact JavaDoc blocks and contains lines beyond the
SE-EDU limit.

Use the standard multiline JavaDoc form and wrap long parser
constants so the project follows the intermediate Java conventions.

Users cannot locate tasks by words in their descriptions.

Add the find command, task-list search, console feedback, and
coverage for matching, no-match, and missing-keyword behavior.

Add the SE-EDU style configuration to Gradle so production and test sources are checked consistently.

Reformat switch expressions and a test lambda to meet the configured rules.
Use a boolean-prefixed name for schedule lookup and clarify Javadocs with consistent terminal punctuation. This resolves the coding-standard nits without changing behavior.

Connect a responsive FXML chat window to Lizzy's existing command and storage flow so users can manage tasks without the console. Keep a separate Launcher entry point for reliable executable JAR startup, while preserving console behavior and regression coverage.
Integrate the tested JavaFX chatbot interface while retaining the increment branch for the course milestone history.
